newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Bucaram faces first rally against reform.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Bucaram faces first rally against reform.

text.p: Ecuador's President Abadala Bucaram faced his first protest rally in five months in power Wednesday when thousands of union followers took to the streets of Quito to oppose his tough economic reforms.
About 5,000 people marched through the center of Quito shouting slogans against Bucaram and his family while students blocked streets and stoned police officers.

The head of the UNE schoolteachers union, Stalin Vargas, told Reuters that Wednesday's protest was just the start of a campaign of protest that would culminate in a general strike together with students, civil servants and energy workers.
"The action plan started with today's protests but we are organizing assemblies all over the country...to define a date for a joint national strike," said Vargas.

Bucaram has prepared a package of economic reforms that include increasing gas and transport subsidies, broadening the tax base, increasing electricity and telephone tariffs by more than 100 percent and at the same time freezing the minimum wage and allowances at about $140 a month.

Bucaram has warned the country that 1997 will be a tough year for Ecuador as it tries to plug a fiscal deficit of about 4.0 percent of gross domestic product. This would create the right conditions for introducing an ambitious plan to peg the sucre to the dollar.
